summary: Select a smallest value without inventing a zero quote.
documentation: min selects the smallest item. A default handles an empty iterable; with no default, empty input raises ValueError. A key function may choose which attribute is compared.
inputs: An iterable and optional default/key arguments.
returns: The smallest item, or the supplied default when empty.
caution: Zero can be a legitimate minimum. Keep a missing result distinct from a real zero-valued quote.
scenarios: Compare delivery quotes for a local order.
Find the earliest available appointment time.
Determine the lowest stock quantity in a category.
title: Find the lowest delivery quote
problem: Input is a list of nonnegative integer prices in cents. Return the smallest quote, or None when the list is empty. A free quote of 0 must remain 0.
goal: Use min() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use None as the empty-list default.
